review.alternative: Metareasoning could occur continuously without explicit partition bounds, though this risks infinite regress in resource usage.
review.would_change_mind: Proof that metareasoning overhead does not degrade real-time execution performance across arbitrary problem classes.

claims.statement: Rational agency requires partitioning costly metareasoning resources between planning solution strategies and executing action plans.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that ideal resource allocation in rational agency must explicitly partition time and effort between metareasoning planning and base-level execution.
support.passage: We shall introduce the metareasoning-partitionproblem—the problem of ideally apportioning costly reasoning resources to planning a solution versus applying resource to executing a solution to a problem.

review.alternative: Purely statistical neural uncertainty estimation might achieve equivalent error detection without explicit symbolic rules.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical evaluation showing neural uncertainty metrics outperforming neuro-symbolic rules under extreme distribution shifts.

claims.statement: Neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks enable effective error detection and correction for predictive models deployed under distribution shifts.

support.explanation: Shows that rule-based symbolic oversight can identify and correct neural model errors when training data differs from operational environments.
support.passage: We provide a neuro-symbolic rule-based framework to conduct error correction and detection of these models to support eventual deployment in security applications.

actions.next_questions: How can autonomous agents dynamically re-partition metareasoning bounds when facing unexpected distribution shifts that invalidate symbolic error rules?
